claims.text: An integrated machine-learning framework combining simulation data and experimental validation can rapidly identify intrinsically strong, ductile, and low-weight RHEA compositions.
Compositional diversity in RHEAs produces variable microstructures.
The proposed ML algorithm is trained on extensive thermo-mechanical simulation data and experimental feedback.
The intended operating conditions are the high-temperature and high-stress conditions typical of refractory applications.
The specific elemental composition determines local lattice distortions.
Local lattice distortions dictate RHEA microstructure and phase stability.
The ML framework learns hidden correlations between multielement composition and strength, ductility, and density.
Learning these correlations enables rapid screening of large compositional spaces for alloys with targeted combinations of strength, ductility, and density.
The framework will identify alloys with higher strength and ductility and lower density than alloys designed using traditional thermo-kinetic or simulation-only approaches.
Traditional simulation-based methods can be too computationally expensive for high-throughput evaluation.
Traditional thermo-kinetic and atomistic or mesoscale methods are less efficient for high-dimensional alloy-composition searches.
Predictions are most reliable within the compositional ranges represented in the training dataset.
Extrapolation to novel elemental combinations far outside the training range may reduce prediction accuracy.
The robustness of the ML predictions in unexplored compositional regions is uncertain.
It is uncertain whether simulation data adequately represent experimental behavior under extreme conditions.
Failure of fabricated candidates to show statistically significant gains in strength and ductility together with lower density relative to conventional benchmarks would falsify the hypothesis.
